# DSH managed OFM 2.8.0

This is a locally managed integration of OFM upstream `999e9f784ea3ea7a11cae383b142697b1ff2c42f` and JetHub upstream `2bf76ce66f1214f18ee3202238fb0f2d02cc791f`, retaining the owner's customized OFM 2.6.0 baseline. It is not an official upstream release-sign artifact. Authentic upstream feed/catalog metadata remains source reference only and does not attest these customized runtime bytes.

The original 22 account providers remain: codearts, buddy, workbuddy, lobsterai, qoder, qodercn, trae, cline, loomy, raccoon, zcode, minimax, minimaxintl, gemini, officeace, accio, autoclaw, autoclawintl, modelscope, astudio, magicrew, codely. The interface additionally exposes qiniu and orcaterm. `aggregate` and `channel-pack-auto` remain internal routes. The embedded duplicate OpenCode account provider is disabled by the OFM product mount; existing OpenCode account records remain intact. The separate OFM anonymous free lane remains available.

Retained custom functions include account pools and credential refs, balance/expiry policies and permanent-credit locks, routing and aggregate/combo selection, token-saving modules and benchmarks, usage ledger/logs, backups and account/model RPCs, gateways/LAN forwarding, shared JetHub backend detection, signed CodeArts transport isolation, Android browser-gesture login, shared SSE and hot reload. The four mobile/client transport functions retain the exact preserved-baseline bytes.

The 2.8 free lane uses the o2a shaping layer, canonical tool declarations/opaque client-tool names, provider-family paths, session/project headers and SSE/error fixes. Qoder queue rotation now tracks the actual request credential, skips malformed accounts, respects model cooldowns and never marks queueing as exhausted credit. Generic channel queue handling precedes native auth/quota error conversion and waits for old stream cancellation before replay. No replay follows emitted model content. Existing stream suppression/recovery code is retained rather than replaced by older upstream copies.

`customization-contract.json` and `src/customization-guard.js` provide read-only source and inheritance checks. The self-updater verifies this contract after signature/staging checks and before changing installed program bytes. Missing channels or changed reviewed mobile/shared-backend interfaces produce a visible rejection while preserving the installed package. Future local managed updates must preserve or explicitly re-review the current contract.

`package.files` includes the full `src` and `adapter` directories. The release runtime does not include the standalone product's web build. Mac and Android do not include a Windows-only Magpie native payload. Android auto transport stays on Node; Bun is not assumed to exist there, and a failed turn is not retried through a second transport. Real upstream login, paid inference, desktop activation and Android installation are separate acceptance steps.


Android login uses host platform capability, not a browser user-agent guess. Domestic AutoClaw opens its actual SMS carrier, international AutoClaw uses the existing Z.ai callback/exchange protocol, and AStudio uses its SMS/password/WeChat carrier. OrcaTerm reuses the phone native WebView cookie bridge; Magicrew uses the phone native same-snapshot localStorage capture and real gateway-key issuance. Native results are bound to the pending account, then saved through the credential service before the interface reports success. Cancellation, deletion and disposal fence late results; cancellation during an asynchronous credential write restores the exact previous value when deduplication targets an existing account. Android never probes desktop browser databases, desktop app files or the Mac keychain. Explicit credential import remains a labeled fallback. Real human authorization on the built phone is still an acceptance step.

The original Mac current-account AutoClaw safeStorage/keychain import is retained, including current-pointer and site ownership checks. The historical `buddy` provider ID and credential refs remain stable while its domestic WorkBuddy account-scoped protocol is preserved. Catalog/control-plane loads leave the inference account-rotation context to avoid nested selection deadlocks.

Balance capability is declared separately for each provider: Codely and Magicrew have real backend balance parsers; ModelScope's actual `/openapi/v1/magicubes/balance` endpoint is wired. Qiniu has no balance/check-in RPC in the verified upstream provider registry and points users to its console; OrcaTerm has no balance/check-in implementation in this integration. Their cards and login/model routes remain available.
